info.name: Rescue Alert System — Production
info.description:
Production API reference for the Rescue Alert System.

## Authentication
All endpoints require a JWT as a Bearer token:
```
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
```

**Quick start:**
1. Set `user_email` and `user_password` in collection variables.
2. Run **JWT Auth → Sign In** — it saves `access_token` and `refresh_token`.
3. All other requests inherit the Bearer token from the collection.

Access tokens last **60 minutes**; run **Refresh Token** to renew them.
New accounts need the `invite_code` configured on the server.

## Variables
| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | API base URL |
| `user_email` | Email or username to sign in with |
| `user_password` | Password for that account |
| `invite_code` | Registration invite code |
| `access_token` | JWT — auto-set by Sign In / Refresh |
| `refresh_token` | Refresh token — auto-set by Sign In |
| `alert_id` | Alert ID for detail/update/delete requests |
| `user_id` | UserProfile ID for detail/update/delete requests |
| `group_id` | Group ID for detail/update/delete requests |
| `message_id` | Message ID for detail/update/delete requests |
| `notification_id` | Notification token record ID |

## Notes
- Registration uses `POST /api/auth/register/`; the invite code is required when configured.
- `sender` on messages and `user` on notifications are set automatically; do not include them in bodies.
- `voice_file` uploads use `multipart/form-data`; do not set `Content-Type` manually.

item.name: Alerts
item.description:
Create and manage rescue alerts. All requests inherit the collection Bearer token.

**Status values:** `OPEN` → `DISPATCHED` → `ACCEPTED` → `IN_PROGRESS` → `RESOLVED` / `CANCELLED`

**Priority values:** `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH`, `CRITICAL`

**Coordinates:** `latitude` must be −90 to 90, `longitude` must be −180 to 180. Both must be provided together on updates.

request.description: Returns all alerts ordered by newest first (`-created_at`).

response.name: 200 OK
response.body:
[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "title": "Fire on Main St",
    "description": "Building fire, multiple floors",
    "latitude": 40.7128,
    "longitude": -74.006,
    "status": "OPEN",
    "priority": "CRITICAL",
    "created_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z"
  }
]

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Fire on Main St",
  "description": "Building fire, multiple floors affected",
  "latitude": 40.7128,
  "longitude": -74.006,
  "status": "OPEN",
  "priority": "CRITICAL"
}

request.description: Create a new alert. `status` defaults to `OPEN`, `priority` defaults to `MEDIUM` if omitted.

item.name: User Profiles
item.description:
Manage user profiles and locations. Django accounts are created automatically on first JWT-authenticated request — there is no separate registration endpoint.

**Role values:** `user` (default), `rescuer`, `admin`

Profile fields exposed: `id`, `username` (JWT UID), `email`, `role`, `latitude`, `longitude`.

request.description: Returns all user profiles.
Returns the profile of the currently authenticated user (derived from the Bearer token).
Update the authenticated user's own profile. Acts as a partial update internally — omitted fields are unchanged.
Update the authenticated user's current GPS coordinates. Both `latitude` and `longitude` are required.
Returns only users that have a non-null `latitude` and `longitude`. Use this to render active users on a map.
Returns the profile of a specific user by their UserProfile `id`.
Replace all fields on a specific user profile. Admin use.
Partially update a specific user profile by ID. Admin use.
Permanently delete a user profile and its associated Django user.

item.name: Groups
item.description: Create and manage user groups (response teams). Group names must be unique. `members` is an array of Django user IDs (the `id` field from UserProfile responses).

request.description: Returns all groups.
Create a new group. `members` is an array of Django User IDs. `members` can be an empty array.
Retrieve a single group by ID.
Replace all fields on a group. The `members` list replaces the existing members entirely.
Partially update a group.
Permanently delete a group. Does not delete the member users.
Add a user to an existing group. `user_id` is the Django User ID (the `id` from a UserProfile response, not the JWT UID).
Remove a user from a group. `user_id` is the Django User ID. Does not delete the user.

item.name: Messages
item.description:
Send and retrieve field messages. Supports text-only or text + voice file attachment.

`sender` is set automatically from the authenticated token — do not include it in request bodies.

Voice files are served from `/media/voices/` and accessible via the `voice_url` field in responses.

request.description: Returns all messages (default ordering).
Returns all messages ordered by `timestamp` descending (newest first). Prefer this over the plain list endpoint.
Create a text message. `text`, `latitude`, and `longitude` are optional. `sender` is set from the token.

response.name: 201 Created
response.body:
{
  "id": 1,
  "sender": {
    "id": 1,
    "username": "<username>",
    "email": "jdoe@example.com",
    "role": "rescuer"
  },
  "title": "Evacuation Update",
  "text": "Sector 3 is clear. All units proceed to sector 4.",
  "voice_file": null,
  "voice_url": null,
  "latitude": 40.7128,
  "longitude": -74.006,
  "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:35:00Z"
}

request.description: Create a message with a voice file attachment. Use `multipart/form-data` — **do not set `Content-Type` manually**, Postman adds the boundary automatically. The response includes `voice_url` pointing to the uploaded file under `/media/voices/`.
Retrieve a single message by ID.
Replace all writable fields on a message. `sender` and `timestamp` are read-only and ignored.
Partially update a message.
Permanently delete a message and its associated voice file.

item.name: Device Registration
item.description:
Register a mobile device for push notifications.

This is the **preferred** endpoint for new integrations. It supports multiple devices per user, platform tagging, and upserts on re-registration (same `user_uid` + `device_id` pair updates the `push_token`).

Authentication is handled by reading the Bearer token directly — not via DRF's `IsAuthenticated`, so a JWT token must still be provided.

request.description:
Register or update a device for push notifications.

**Required fields:** `push_token`, `device_id`, `platform`

**platform options:** `android`, `ios`, `other`

**device_model:** Optional. Human-readable device name.

If the same `device_id` is already registered for this JWT user the `push_token` is updated (upsert). Returns 204 on success.

response.name: 400 Bad Request — missing required fields

item.name: Notifications (Legacy)
item.description:
Simple push notification token store. One token per record, not per device.

**Prefer Device Registration** for new integrations — it supports multi-device per user and push upsert.

`user` is set automatically from the authenticated token and is read-only.

request.description: Returns all registered notification token records.
Register a push notification token. `user` is set from the token. Tokens must be globally unique — re-registering the same token returns 400.
Retrieve a single notification token record by ID.
Update a notification token record with a new push token.
Remove a notification token record.
